subject.title: RFC: Standard Hosting Profiles and Ready Check

question: Should OpenClaw promote existing readiness and configuration facts into named, release-tested hosting-profile contracts, beginning with only the local readiness foundation or with the full four-profile matrix?
rationale: The implementation seams exist, but choosing which runtime shapes become durable support promises and which existing deployments may begin failing readiness requires explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept the local foundation
options.body: Approve the canonical condition/result schema and backward-compatible local projection first, with later decisions for container, reverse-proxy, node-mode, and release gating.

options.title: Accept the full matrix
options.body: Approve all four profiles, strict selection rules, node-mode predicates, and package-acceptance gating as one support contract.

options.title: Retain unprofiled readiness
options.body: Improve general core readiness facts while leaving named hosting-shape validation and support matrices downstream.

recommendation.title: Accept the local foundation
recommendation.body: Approve the canonical condition/result schema and backward-compatible local projection first, with later decisions for container, reverse-proxy, node-mode, and release gating.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing public probe behavior and its redaction boundary are the central compatibility and security surfaces that this RFC proposes to expand.
